response.query: How can co-design with sampled students be operationalized (recruitment, compensation, advisory roles, translation) to ensure equity and avoid stigmatizing measures?
response.answer: Co-design with sampled students should involve diverse recruitment, fair compensation, defined advisory roles, and clear translation of feedback to ensure equity and avoid stigmatizing measures. Use transparent processes and equitable incentives.

results.title: Medicare Program; End-Stage Renal Disease Prospective ...
results.content: *ESRDPayment@cms.hhs.gov*, for issues related to the ESRD PPS and coverage and payment for renal dialysis services furnished to individuals with acute kidney injury (AKI). This rule finalizes changes related to the End-Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) Prospective Payment System (PPS), payment for renal dialysis services furnished to individuals with acute kidney injury (AKI), the ESRD Quality Incentive Program (QIP), and the ESRD Treatment Choices (ETC) Model. On January 1, 2011, we implemented the ESRD PPS, a case-mix adjusted, bundled PPS for renal dialysis services furnished by ESRD facilities as required by section 1881(b)(14) of the Social Security Act (the Act), as added by section 153(b) of the Medicare Improvements for Patients and Providers Act of 2008 (MIPPA) (Pub. L. 111-148), established that beginning calendar year (CY) 2012, and each subsequent year, the Secretary of the Department of Health and Human Services (the Secretary) shall annually increase payment amounts by an ESRD market basket increase factor, reduced by the productivity adjustment described in section 1886(b)(3)(B)(xi)(II) of the Act. This rule updates the ESRD PPS for CY 2023.
